newsitem.title: USA: West U.S. hydropower seen ample despite dry summer.
newsitem.headline: West U.S. hydropower seen ample despite dry summer.

text.p: Water supplies in the western U.S. remained ample for hydroelectric generation through the end of 1996 despite a dry summer, utilities and government agencies said.

The Army Corps of Engineers and Bureau of Reclamation, which operate the mammoth hydroelectric system in the Pacific Northwest, downplayed any significant effect of a parched summer on power output for the rest of the year.
In the past three months, total rainfall in the Northwest was approximately 50 percent below normal.
